claims.text: We tokenized for the bag anyway, so the abstract fingerprint was free here -- donate it so renamed_clusters need not re-abstract the same source.
claims.why: The claim refers to 'renamed_clusters' which is not defined in this chunk; the donation via memo.put_abstract_fp is visible but the benefit cannot be verified.

claims.text: Whichever pass runs first pays; the other rides along.
claims.why: The claim describes a global execution order not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Rare tokens = those not saturating the corpus (drop ID/NUM/STR/common ops).
claims.why: The claim mentions dropping ID/NUM/STR/common ops, but the code only filters by document frequency; the actual token set is not shown.
The claim states that identical fingerprints are handled elsewhere; no code in this chunk handles them.

claims.text: only incidental overlap -> not a real near-clone
claims.why: The claim interprets min_shared_rare as filtering incidental overlap, but the exact semantics depend on external constants.

Edge overlaps are only recorded when union succeeds; if union is skipped due to size cap, no edge is added, so a component with only such skipped edges would have no overlaps and be skipped. The comment says 'component held only cap-skipped edges' which is consistent with the code: if all candidate pairs were skipped by cap, no edge_overlap entries exist, so overlaps list is empty and component is skipped.
The string literal is returned as the safety value when hits exist.

observations.what: union cap uses max_cluster from outer scope; may be undefined if not passed
union uses keep_root based on index order (ra < rb), not size; may create unbalanced trees
find uses path compression, but union does not compress after linking; acceptable for small sets
_safety returns 'safety': None when no hits; callers may expect a string or None
Import of GENERIC_HIGH_RISK_PATHS is inside function; exception silent
